review_candidates.description: We are Europe's research laboratory for the life sciences – an intergovernmental organisation performing scientific research in disciplines including molecular biology, physics, chemistry and computer science. We are an international, innovative and interdisciplinary laboratory with more than 1800 employees from many nations, operating across six sites, in Heidelberg (HQ), Barcelona, Hinxton near Cambridge, Hamburg, Grenoble and Rome. As our Precision Mechanic, you contribute to the development and maintenance of scientific instrumentation by providing specialist precision manufacturing expertise within the mechanical workshop. Working closely with engineers and researchers, you advise on production designs, manufacture precision mechanical components, and support the assembly, repair and functional improvement of mechanical instruments. You will contribute to effective operation and organisation of the workshop and timely delivery of high-quality manufactured components. Aufgaben Produce precision mechanical components of scientific instrumentation using a range of machining and fabrication tools, with particular expertise in turned parts. Support research groups in the repair and functional improvement of existing mechanical components. Advise designers on the manufacturability and performance of mechanical design. Coordinate regular maintenance, repair, and replacement of workshop equipment. Coordinate the availability and restocking of materials and tooling for the workshop. Build and maintain relationships with external materials and tooling suppliers and contract workshops. Advise on ongoing modernisation efforts within the mechanical workshop. Capabilities You build effective working relationships with colleagues and stakeholders. You communicate information clearly and professionally. You take ownership of responsibilities and deliver outcomes within agreed timeframes, including under occasional time pressure. Problem Solving: You identify challenges and apply sound technical judgement to determine appropriate and effective solutions. You respond positively to changing priorities and organisational requirements and demonstrate openness to learning new skills to meet evolving project and organisational needs. Profil Technical training in mechanical engineering and relevant experience producing precision mechanical components in a professional mechanical workshop environment Extensive expertise in producing turned parts on both conventional and CNC lathes, from a range of materials, including metals, plastics Experience in quality control for tooling and manufactured components Experience maintaining workshop machines Demonstrated experience with modern CAD, CAM, and CNC software Very good technical communication skills in both English and German (minimum B2 level) You may also have Experience producing milled parts on both conventional and CNC milling machines Qualifications or experience supervising and training colleagues or trainees in mechanical workshop environment Experience in plastic shaping techniques and plastic adhesive procedures. Experience supporting or coordinating mechanical workshop operations Wir bieten EMBL is curiosity-driven, community-oriented and international. As an inclusive, equal opportunity employer, we believe that diversity enables us to collaborate more effectively and be innovative in our approaches. We are, therefore, committed to creating an inclusive and flexible culture - one where everyone can realise their full potential and make a positive contribution to our organisation. We encourage applications from individuals who can complement our existing team – we believe that success is built on having teams whose backgrounds and personal experiences reflect the diversity of the populations that our science serves. We actively encourage applications from all genders and cultures, ethnic groups and all demographics to help us avoid perpetuating biases and oversights at this transformational point in our people strategy. Enjoy lots of benefits: Financial incentives: Salary free of income tax, Monthly family, child and non-resident allowances, annual salary review, pension scheme, death benefit, long-term care, accident-at-work and unemployment insurances Flexible working arrangements Private medical insurance for you and your immediate family (including all prescriptions and generous dental & optical cover) Generous time off: 30 days annual leave per year, in addition to public holidays Relocation package including installation grant (if applicable) Campus life: Free shuttle bus (Heidelberg), library, subsidised on-site cafeteria, casual dress code, extensive sports and social club activities (on campus and remotely) Family benefits: Kindergarten (Heidelberg), 10 days of child sick leave, generous paid maternity/parental leave and monthly family & child allowances Benefits for international newcomers: Visa exemption, education grant for private schooling, financial support to travel back to your home country every second year and a monthly non-resident allowance. For detailed information please visit our employee benefits page here What else you need to know International applicants: We recruit internationally and successful candidates are offered visa exemptions. Visit our International Applicants page, to find out more. EMBL is a signatory of DORA. Find out how we apply DORA principles to our recruitment and performance assessment processes here. Diversity and inclusion: At EMBL, we believe that diverse teams drive innovation and scientific excellence. We encourage applications from candidates of all genders, identities, nationalities and/or any other diverse backgrounds. How to apply: To apply please submit a cover letter and a CV through our online system. Applications will close at 23:59 CET on the date shown below. We aim to provide a response within two weeks after the closing date. Important note Please be advised that a valid work permit for Germany is required for non-EU citizens. Unfortunately, applications without a valid work permit and sufficient German language skills may not be considered. LNKD1_DE

review_candidates.title: Plant Engineer - Mechanical
review_candidates.description: Title: Plant Engineer - Mechanical Location: New Florence, PA 15944 Salary: $140,000 - $160,000 Established in 2015, we are a power-generation operator that manages a state-of-the-art coal-fired waste facility built in 2004, employing roughly 135 people to support reliable baseload energy for the PJM grid. As the largest waste-coal plant in the U.S., we produce enough electricity for 650,000+ homes while reducing regional environmental impact through CFB combustion and mine-land reclamation. As we continue to grow, our facility in New Florence is seeking a Plant Engineer - Mechanical to support continuous operations by providing technical expertise for rotating and stationary equipment, project oversight, and hands-on troubleshooting with operations and maintenance teams. What You Will Be Doing Serve as the primary technical resource for mechanical systems, including stationary and rotating equipment, piping, boilers, turbine generators, and auxiliary machinery Investigate, diagnose, and resolve plant operating, safety, and mechanical issues to support continuous, reliable, and efficient power-plant operations Develop and implement procedures, predictive/preventive maintenance plans, and reliability improvement solutions to reduce maintenance costs and equipment failures Provide hands-on troubleshooting and technical guidance to operations, maintenance teams, and contractors, supporting daily plant needs and project execution Plan and support outages, including work scoping, equipment refurbishment, parts re-engineering, and analysis through vibration, oil, and performance monitoring What You Need for This Position Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering or related field 5+ years of power-plant or heavy industrial experience involving boilers, steam-cycle equipment, rotating machinery, and mechanical systems Hands-on expertise with pumps, fans, blowers, compressors, motors, gearboxes, and mechanical components such as bearings, seals, and couplings Strong ability to diagnose and troubleshoot complex mechanical issues, including vibration analysis, oil analysis, outage planning, and equipment refurbishment Knowledge of industrial codes and standards (API, ASME, ANSI, OSHA) What's In It for You Full benefits package (Medical, Dental, Vision, Life, LTD/STD, 401k with matching) and more!
